subject: Request: transient accelerator cushion + non-standard overage cap for NebulaCore
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@nebulacore.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@nebulacore.com, Elena Park <elena.park@nebulacore.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Temporary accelerator substitution + pricing cushion request

Hi Kimberly,

Quick ask from our side — we need to temporarily move ~20% of our reserved capacity (reserved as RTX-A6000 class) into a lower-latency, lower-memory instance family while we finish an on-prem migration. The short version: a supplier delay dropped availability for 3 weeks and we're at risk of missing our SLA to a handful of customers.

We want Redwood to:
- Allow a transient substitution of up to 20% of our reserved GPUs to the older RTX-A5000 family for a 21-day window (no change to aggregate vCPU/RAM allocation)
- Cap overage/shortfall charges on that substituted capacity at a fixed blended rate (we propose $1.85/GPU-hour) for the 21 days
- Keep reservation hold (no cancellation charges) for the affected pool while this substitution is active

We can sign a short addendum and will provide a smoke performance file (attached) showing expected token throughput degradation but acceptable tail latency for our use case. If possible, we'd appreciate an expedited approval since our customer runway is tight.

Thanks —
Sanjay
Head of Engineering, NebulaCore

Attachments: MA_plan_v2.pdf (proposal), transient-performance-smoke.csv (perf samples)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Deal Desk <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Temporary accelerator substitution + pricing cushion request — need exec signoff

Team — forwarding NebulaCore's ask. Key points:
- 20% transient substitution (A6000 -> A5000 family) for 21 days
- Proposed blended overage cap $1.85/GPU-hour (they're asking)
- Reservation hold and no cancellation fee for affected capacity during window

Proposed commercial response from our side (draft):
1) Approve transient substitution for up to 21 days with instrumentation and KPIs enabled.
2) Offer a one-time transient concession: blended overage cap of $1.65/GPU-hour for the substituted portion.
3) Require NebulaCore to accept a 10% transient discount on the substituted hours in exchange for the cap.
4) Add a strict end date and an automatic reflow to their original reserved SKU after 21 days; no structural contract change.

Asking for quick exec signoff on the concession + any limits we should place (e.g., hard cap on total hours, SLA carve-outs). I can take the doc to legal for a 1-page addendum once approved.

--
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Temporary accelerator substitution + pricing cushion request — need exec signoff

Kimberly,

From an infra perspective a few notes:
- Substituting A6000 -> A5000 family will likely reduce peak throughput ~18-25% depending on model mix (their attached smoke shows this). Fine for many inference workloads but we should require pre/post smoke traces.
- We should require KV cache warming and an engineering rollback plan in case latency spikes > 95th pct thresholds.
- Suggest adding a 200-hour soft cap on substituted hours for the 21-day window per reserved pool to limit abuse (they're asking for 20% of reserved; this soft cap makes it bounded).

Commercially, $1.65/GPU-hour seems reasonable if we enforce the telemetry hooks and the rollback plan. If we don't get instrumentation, we should default back to standard overage rates.

I'll add a sentence for the addendum: "Customer shall enable Redwood tracing and token-level latency logs for substituted instances for the duration of the concession window."

— Marcus
Principal Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@nebulacore.com>, Elena Park <elena.park@nebulacore.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Temporary accelerator substitution + pricing cushion request — approval (conditions)

Approved with conditions (executive sign-off):
1) Approve transient substitution for up to 21 calendar days for up to 20% of the reserved pool.
2) One-time blended overage cap of $1.65/GPU-hour on substituted capacity for the concession window.
3) NebulaCore agrees to a 10% transient usage discount applied to substituted hours in exchange for the cap.
4) Enforce a 200-hour soft cap per affected reserved pool for substituted hours; Redwood will notify if the cap is approached.
5) Telemetry & rollback: customer must enable Redwood tracing and 95th percentile latency alerts; failure to enable triggers immediate reversion to standard SKUs and rates.
6) Legal addendum: 1-page amendment signed via DocuSign; concession expires automatically at window end and cannot be extended without fresh exec approval.
7) Finance note: revenue impact estimated ~$9.6k net concession — finance to record under transient concessions (code TC-2028-Q1).

Kimberly — you have signoff to proceed with the addendum and DocuSign flow. Marcus — please work with their ops on the telemetry hookup. Aditya — please include the cap in the billing delta and flag finance code.

Lauren Bishop
VP, Deal Desk (Acting)
